expertise.title: Diabetes & Lifestyle Disease Management
expertise.summary: A personal plan for blood sugar, daily habits, and long-term well-being.
expertise.body:
Diabetes means blood glucose is persistently too high. Care looks beyond a single reading to your symptoms, medical history, daily routine, and related health risks.

Dr. Meghana’s approach combines individual attention, evidence-based treatment, and practical lifestyle support. Consultation can help you understand your results, discuss your concerns, and plan ongoing review.

Bring recent glucose reports, your current prescriptions, and any home readings. The care plan may include nutrition, activity, monitoring, and medication, based on your individual needs.

faqs.question: Can I have diabetes without symptoms?
faqs.answer: Yes. Some people have no obvious symptoms; blood tests are used to assess diabetes.

faqs.question: Is everyone given the same treatment?
faqs.answer: No. Treatment and monitoring depend on the type of diabetes and your personal health needs.

faqs.question: Should I stop medication when readings improve?
faqs.answer: Discuss changes with your treating doctor; an improved reading alone is not a reason to stop prescribed treatment.

expertise.title: Hypertension & Cardiovascular Health
expertise.summary: Care for blood pressure and the health of your heart.
expertise.body:
High blood pressure can be present without obvious symptoms. Repeated, correctly taken measurements help your doctor understand whether it needs treatment.

A consultation considers your readings alongside your health history, medicines, and lifestyle. Dr. Meghana provides personalised care and follow-up, with attention to cardiovascular well-being.

Bring your blood pressure record and a list of medicines. Discuss realistic changes to food, activity, and other habits, as well as any medication questions.

faqs.question: Will I always feel high blood pressure?
faqs.answer: No. Many people feel well even when their blood pressure is high.

faqs.question: Does one high reading confirm hypertension?
faqs.answer: An isolated reading needs context. Your doctor may recommend repeat measurements and further assessment.

faqs.question: When is urgent care needed?
faqs.answer: Chest pain, severe breathlessness, or sudden weakness or difficulty speaking need emergency assessment. Do not wait for an online appointment.

expertise.title: Thyroid Disorders
expertise.summary: Understand your thyroid and find a treatment plan that fits you.
expertise.body:
The thyroid produces hormones that influence many body functions. An underactive thyroid can cause tiredness, sensitivity to cold, or weight changes, but these symptoms can also have other causes.

Thyroid care begins with your symptoms, history, and appropriate blood tests. Dr. Meghana offers personalised evaluation and ongoing management of thyroid-related conditions.

Bring previous thyroid reports and details of medicines or supplements. Follow-up helps assess your response and whether your plan needs adjustment.

faqs.question: Can symptoms alone confirm a thyroid disorder?
faqs.answer: No. Blood tests and clinical assessment help distinguish thyroid problems from other causes.

faqs.question: Will I need repeated tests?
faqs.answer: Your doctor decides when to repeat tests based on the condition and treatment.

faqs.question: What if I am planning pregnancy?
faqs.answer: Tell your doctor before pregnancy, as thyroid assessment and treatment may need closer attention.

expertise.title: Adult Immunization
expertise.summary: Protection tailored to your age, health, and daily life.
expertise.body:
Vaccination is relevant throughout adulthood. Recommendations depend on your age, medical conditions, previous vaccination history, work, travel, and pregnancy status.

Dr. Meghana offers an individual vaccination review. Bring any vaccine records and mention allergies or reactions to earlier doses, so that the discussion is based on your own circumstances.

The consultation can clarify which vaccines are appropriate and how follow-up doses should be planned. Recommendations are adapted to local guidance and individual needs.

faqs.question: Are vaccines only for children?
faqs.answer: No. Adults may need routine vaccines, boosters, or vaccines for particular risks.

faqs.question: What if I cannot find my records?
faqs.answer: Tell the doctor which vaccines you remember receiving and approximately when.

faqs.question: Can I discuss travel vaccines?
faqs.answer: Yes. Share your destination and travel date early, so that any required planning can be discussed.

expertise.title: Preventive & Wellness Medicine
expertise.summary: Make space for your health before concerns become bigger.
expertise.body:
Preventive care is a conversation about your health today and the changes you want to make for tomorrow. It considers your history, family health, existing conditions, and daily routine.

Dr. Meghana encourages awareness, patient education, and sustainable lifestyle choices. A personalised review can help identify what deserves attention and which health goals are practical for you.

Bring your previous reports and a few questions you would like answered. The discussion should help you leave with a clearer understanding of the next steps.

faqs.question: Does everyone need the same check-up package?
faqs.answer: No. Discuss which assessments are relevant to your individual history and concerns.

faqs.question: Can I attend without a current illness?
faqs.answer: Yes. Preventive consultations provide an opportunity to discuss health goals and risk factors.

faqs.question: What should I discuss?
faqs.answer: Share your daily routine, family history, ongoing medicines, and the health changes that matter to you.

expertise.title: Infectious & Tropical Diseases
expertise.summary: Thoughtful evaluation of infections and related concerns.
expertise.body:
Infections can have many causes, so your symptoms, their timing, and any recent travel or exposure are important parts of the discussion.

Dr. Meghana’s general medicine care includes infectious and tropical diseases. Evaluation is personalised rather than based on symptoms alone, with investigations and follow-up guided by your clinical needs.

For example, dengue is spread by infected mosquitoes and can range from a mild illness to a serious condition. Severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, or bleeding require urgent assessment.

faqs.question: Do all infections need antibiotics?
faqs.answer: No. Treatment depends on the cause; avoid choosing antibiotics without medical advice.

faqs.question: What information is useful?
faqs.answer: Note when symptoms started, any travel, similar illness around you, and medicines already taken.

faqs.question: Do I need tests before visiting?
faqs.answer: Share any existing reports. Further tests should be selected after an appropriate assessment.

expertise.title: Evaluation of Fever
expertise.summary: A clear assessment of the symptoms behind a fever.
expertise.body:
A fever is a symptom, not a complete diagnosis. Your doctor considers how long it has lasted, other symptoms, your medical history, and examination findings.

Dr. Meghana offers individual evaluation, with investigations and follow-up chosen according to the clinical picture. Keep a record of temperature readings and medicines taken if available.

Do not rely only on the temperature coming down to judge recovery. In dengue, warning signs can appear after fever improves. Persistent vomiting, bleeding, or severe abdominal pain need urgent care.

faqs.question: What should I bring?
faqs.answer: Bring recent reports, prescriptions, and a short timeline of symptoms.

faqs.question: Is every fever dengue?
faqs.answer: No. There are many possible causes. Assessment and appropriately timed tests help clarify the diagnosis.

faqs.question: Can I message for an emergency?
faqs.answer: WhatsApp is for consultation enquiries. Seek emergency care for severe or rapidly worsening symptoms.

expertise.title: Medical Disorders in Pregnancy
expertise.summary: Medical care coordinated around mother and baby.
expertise.body:
Existing medical conditions and new concerns during pregnancy deserve individual attention. Tell your healthcare team about your medical history, current prescriptions, supplements, and pregnancy plans.

Dr. Meghana’s physician services include medical disorders in pregnancy, alongside care from your obstetric team. The aim is a coordinated plan that takes your circumstances and ongoing maternity care into account.

Bring antenatal records and relevant reports. Questions about blood pressure, diabetes, thyroid conditions, or medication should be discussed directly with your treating doctors.

faqs.question: Does a physician replace my obstetrician?
faqs.answer: No. Medical care is coordinated with your obstetric and maternity team.

faqs.question: Should I mention a condition before pregnancy?
faqs.answer: Yes. Discuss existing conditions and medicines when planning pregnancy.

faqs.question: Can I change a prescription myself?
faqs.answer: Speak with your treating doctors before changing or stopping prescribed medication.

expertise.title: Geriatrics
expertise.summary: Personalised support for health, function, and independence.
expertise.body:
Health needs in later life vary widely. A useful review considers not only medical conditions but also daily function, mobility, hearing, vision, and the support available at home.

Dr. Meghana offers attentive care for older adults, including discussion of ongoing conditions, medicines, and personal priorities. The approach recognises the individual behind the medical record.

Bring a current medication list and earlier reports. A family member or caregiver can join the discussion if the patient wishes.

faqs.question: What is the focus of geriatric care?
faqs.answer: Supporting well-being and everyday function while addressing the person’s medical needs.

faqs.question: Can a family member attend?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the patient is comfortable with their participation.

faqs.question: What helps prepare for the visit?
faqs.answer: Write down changes in daily activities, current concerns, and all medicines being taken.

blogs.title: Make the most of your first visit
blogs.summary: A simple way to organise your questions and records.
blogs.body:
A consultation is your time to talk about what matters to you. Start by writing down your main concern and when it began. Note any changes you have noticed and the questions you would most like answered.

Keep previous reports, prescriptions, and your medicine list together. If you already record blood pressure or glucose at home, bring those records too.

Before leaving, ask what the next step is and how to arrange a follow-up. If any part of the discussion is unclear, ask for it to be explained again. Clear communication is part of good care.

blogs.title: Your health, your questions
blogs.summary: Make room for the conversation behind the consultation.
blogs.body:
It can be easy to forget a question during an appointment. A short list helps keep the conversation focused on the things that affect your everyday life.

You might want to ask what a test is intended to show, how a care plan fits your routine, or when a follow-up is needed. Share practical concerns such as work schedules or difficulty understanding a prescription.

A trusted family member can help take notes if you would like support. Your preferences and questions are useful parts of the discussion.

blogs.title: Keep your follow-up simple
blogs.summary: Bring your progress and questions into one place.
blogs.body:
A follow-up visit is a chance to review what has changed since your last consultation. Keep the previous care plan and any new reports together so that the conversation has a clear starting point.

Write down questions about your medicines, daily routine, or any new concerns. Describe what is working well and what is proving difficult.

Confirm the next appointment and any tests your doctor has requested. For urgent symptoms, seek appropriate medical care instead of waiting for a routine follow-up.

articles.title: Understanding diabetes
articles.summary: A starting point for understanding blood glucose and ongoing care.
articles.body:
Diabetes affects how the body handles blood glucose. Some people notice thirst, tiredness, or changes in vision; others have no obvious symptoms.

A care plan considers glucose results alongside blood pressure, cholesterol, everyday habits, and prescribed treatment. Your doctor can explain what your results mean and decide when you need follow-up.

The NIDDK overview below provides further background on diabetes and its management.

articles.title: Why blood pressure matters
articles.summary: High blood pressure can be present even when you feel well.
articles.body:
High blood pressure often has no noticeable symptoms. Measuring it is an important part of understanding cardiovascular health.

Your doctor interprets readings in context and can discuss treatment and lifestyle changes suited to you. Bring any home records to the consultation rather than relying on memory.

The World Health Organization’s overview below explains the condition in more detail.

articles.title: Understanding thyroid symptoms
articles.summary: Why an assessment matters more than symptoms alone.
articles.body:
Thyroid symptoms can overlap with other health conditions. Tiredness or weight changes alone cannot tell you whether your thyroid is underactive.

A clinical assessment and blood tests help clarify the cause. Bring previous results and medicine details to your visit so that any changes can be reviewed.

Read the NIDDK resource below for more about hypothyroidism.
